historical_claims.anchor: This is Amazing Fantasy number fifteen, the comic that introduced Peter Parker in 1962.
Amazing Fantasy was an anthology of short speculative tales, not an established Spider-Man series.
The Library of Congress now preserves the original Amazing Fantasy pages.
Spider-Man is credited to Lee and Ditko, whose contributions were substantial but not identical.
Accounts of early development also involve Jack Kirby, who drew the published cover; Ditko drew the origin story inside.
historical_claims.source_locator: cover credit; earlier designs discussed in history

historical_claims.anchor: A criminal runs past Peter. Peter can stop him. Peter doesn't.
In the 1962 story, the lesson about great power and great responsibility is given in a concluding narrator's caption.
On one page, Lee asks Ditko to alter the appearance of a car and its passengers, an instruction visible in the original art but not in the published panel.
